books.title: Atomic Habits
books.author: James Clear
books.description: An easy and proven way to build good habits and break bad ones through tiny changes that deliver remarkable results.

books.title: Project Hail Mary
books.author: Andy Weir
books.description: A lone astronaut must save humanity from extinction — but he can't remember why he was sent.

books.title: The Midnight Library
books.author: Matt Haig
books.description: Between life and death is a library, and within that library, the shelves go on forever.

books.title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
books.author: Yuval Noah Harari
books.description: A sweeping narrative of humanity from the Stone Age to the twenty-first century.

books.title: The Name of the Wind
books.author: Patrick Rothfuss
books.description: The riveting first-person narrative of Kvothe, a young man who grows to become the most notorious wizard his world has ever seen.

books.title: Educated
books.author: Tara Westover
books.description: A memoir about a young girl who, kept out of school, leaves her survivalist family and goes on to earn a PhD from Cambridge.

books.title: Gone Girl
books.author: Gillian Flynn
books.description: On a warm summer morning in Missouri, it is Nick and Amy Dunne's fifth wedding anniversary — and Amy has disappeared.

books.title: The Song of Achilles
books.author: Madeline Miller
books.description: A tale of gods, kings, immortal fame, and the human heart, retelling the story of the Iliad.

books.title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
books.author: Daniel Kahneman
books.description: A tour of the mind explaining the two systems that drive the way we think — one fast and intuitive, the other slow and deliberate.

books.title: The Long Field
books.author: Pamela Petro
books.description: A memoir of place and belonging that wanders through Wales, America, and the landscapes we carry with us.

books.title: Cloud Cuckoo Land
books.author: Anthony Doerr
books.description: An intricate, time-spanning novel about a lost ancient text and the readers who protect it across centuries.

books.title: The Anthropocene Reviewed
books.author: John Green
books.description: Essays that review human experiences on a five-star scale, from the QWERTY keyboard to the Lascaux cave paintings.

books.title: A Line Made by Walking
books.author: Sara Baume
books.description: A quiet, precise novel about an artist retreating to her deceased grandmother's rural cottage to find a new way of seeing.

books.title: The Overstory
books.author: Richard Powers
books.description: EpA sweeping novel about nine Americans whose unique life experiences with trees bring them together to address the destruction of forests.

books.title: Ways of Seeing
books.author: John Berger
books.description: A landmark book on how we view art, advertising, and the images that surround us in modern life.

books.title: Dune
books.author: Frank Herbert
books.description: The epic story of Paul Atreides on the desert planet Arrakis, where spice, politics, and prophecy collide.

books.title: The Design of Everyday Things
books.author: Don Norman
books.description: A foundational guide to user-centered design, showing how the objects around us reveal the principles of good and bad design.

books.title: The Law of the Sublime
books.author: Robert Greene
books.description: From the author of The 48 Laws of Power: a guide to the sublime — the moments of awe that break us out of the narrow circle of everyday consciousness — drawn from science, history, art, and nature, with practical exercises in every chapter. Greene wrote it over seven years following his stroke.

books.title: Carry More Without Breaking
books.author: Benjamin Lavoie
books.description: For the man who's holding it all together — family, work, money, responsibility — but quietly burning out. A guide to carrying more of life's load without breaking under it. (Description drafted from the book's cover copy.)

books.title: The Negro Motorist Green Book Compendium
books.author: Victor H. Green
books.description: Four complete editions of Victor Green's landmark travel guide — 1938, 1947, 1954, and 1963–64 — reproduced in one volume: the hotels, restaurants, garages, and businesses where Black travelers could safely stop, eat, and sleep in segregated America, decade by decade.

books.title: The Dictator's Handbook
books.author: Bruce Bueno de Mesquita & Alastair Smith
books.description: Bueno de Mesquita and Smith argue that leaders in every system survive by satisfying the small coalition that keeps them in power, which is why bad behavior is so often good politics.

books.title: The Denial of Death
books.author: Ernest Becker
books.description: Becker's Pulitzer Prize–winning argument that the awareness of death is the central fact of human psychology, and that culture, heroism, and achievement are built to deny it.

books.title: The Status Game
books.author: Will Storr
books.description: Storr examines how humans compete for status through games of dominance, virtue, and success, and how that competition shapes groups, politics, and everyday life.

books.title: The Farther Reaches of Human Nature
books.author: Abraham H. Maslow
books.description: Published after his death, Maslow's final book extends his work on human motivation into self-actualization, peak experiences, and the farther reaches of human growth.

books.title: The Courage to Be Disliked
books.author: Ichiro Kishimi & Fumitake Koga
books.description: In a series of dialogues between a philosopher and a young man, Kishimi and Koga present Alfred Adler's psychology as a case that freedom and happiness do not depend on other people's approval.

books.title: Understanding Human Nature
books.author: Alfred Adler
books.description: Drawn from Adler's public lectures in Vienna, this is his own introduction to individual psychology: how inferiority, striving, and early experience form personality and character.

books.title: Man and His Symbols
books.author: Carl G. Jung
books.description: Jung and four of his closest associates introduce his psychology of the unconscious, dreams, and symbols in an illustrated volume written for general readers.

books.title: The Origins and History of Consciousness
books.author: Erich Neumann
books.description: Neumann, one of Jung's leading students, uses world mythology to trace how individual consciousness develops through the same archetypal stages as human consciousness as a whole.

books.title: Good Strategy Bad Strategy
books.author: Richard Rumelt
books.description: Rumelt separates real strategy from buzzwords and ambition: a good strategy is a kernel of diagnosis, guiding policy, and coherent action aimed at the crux of a challenge.

books.title: The Strategy Paradox
books.author: Michael E. Raynor
books.description: Raynor's paradox: the strategies with the greatest chance of success also carry the greatest chance of failure, because both demand total commitment to an uncertain future — and his answer is managing that uncertainty deliberately.

books.title: Playing to Win
books.author: A.G. Lafley and Roger L. Martin
books.description: The playbook Lafley and Martin used at Procter & Gamble: strategy is five integrated choices — a winning aspiration, where to play, how to win, the capabilities required, and the management systems to sustain them.

books.title: Competitive Strategy
books.author: Michael E. Porter
books.description: Porter's founding text of modern strategy: the Five Forces that shape an industry's structure, and the three generic strategies — cost leadership, differentiation, focus — for positioning inside it.

books.title: The Innovator's Dilemma
books.author: Clayton M. Christensen
books.description: Christensen shows how excellent companies can do everything right — listen to their best customers, invest in the highest margins — and still be undone by cheaper, simpler disruptive technologies entering from below.

books.title: The Three Rules
books.author: Michael E. Raynor and Mumtaz Ahmed
books.description: From 45 years of data on 25,000 companies, Raynor and Ahmed find that exceptional performers follow three rules: better before cheaper, revenue before cost — and there are no other rules.

books.title: The Lords of Strategy
books.author: Walter Kiechel
books.description: Kiechel's history of how corporate strategy was invented — through Bruce Henderson at BCG, Bill Bain, Fred Gluck at McKinsey, and Michael Porter — and how it launched the modern consulting industry.

books.title: The McKinsey Way
books.author: Ethan M. Rasiel
books.description: A former McKinsey associate lays out the firm's working method: hypothesis-driven, MECE-structured problem solving, the 80/20 rule, and how the world's most secretive consultancy thinks through a client's problem.

books.title: Letters from a Stoic
books.author: Seneca
books.description: Late in his life, Seneca wrote 124 letters to his friend Lucilius on how to live: time, death, wealth, friendship, and self-command. This Penguin selection of forty of them is the classic English entry point.

books.title: Discourses and Selected Writings
books.author: Epictetus
books.description: Epictetus, born enslaved and later freed, taught that freedom is internal: his student Arrian transcribed these lectures on what is and is not in our power, and this edition adds the Enchiridion, his handbook.

books.title: On Obligations
books.author: Cicero
books.description: Written in the last year of his life and addressed to his son, Cicero's De Officiis sets out what a person in public life owes: to justice, to country, and to their own character when duty and advantage collide.

books.title: The Inner Citadel
books.author: Pierre Hadot
books.description: Hadot's landmark study of Marcus Aurelius's Meditations shows the notebook for what it was: not a diary but a discipline — spiritual exercises built on Epictetus's three disciplines of desire, action, and assent.

books.title: Courage Under Fire
books.author: James B. Stockdale
books.description: Vice Admiral James Stockdale, shot down over North Vietnam in 1965, spent seven and a half years as the senior POW in the Hanoi Hilton. This short book — its full title is Testing Epictetus's Doctrines in a Laboratory of Human Behavior — is his account of how the Enchiridion he had memorized carried him and the men he led through it.

books.title: A Guide to the Good Life
books.author: William B. Irvine
books.description: A philosophy professor's modern manual for Stoic practice — negative visualization, the dichotomy of control, voluntary discomfort — aimed at its original goal: not suppressing joy but securing it.

books.title: How to Be a Stoic
books.author: Massimo Pigliucci
books.description: A philosopher works through Stoicism in imagined conversation with Epictetus himself — the disciplines of desire, action, and assent translated into a program for modern life.

books.title: How to Think Like a Roman Emperor
books.author: Donald Robertson
books.description: A cognitive-behavioral therapist tells the life of Marcus Aurelius as a worked example — each chapter pairs an episode from the emperor's life with the Stoic practice he used to meet it.

books.title: The Obstacle Is the Way
books.author: Ryan Holiday
books.description: Holiday retells Marcus Aurelius's line — the impediment to action advances action — through stories of Rockefeller, Amelia Earhart, Ulysses S. Grant, and Steve Jobs: perception, action, and will as a formula for turning trials into triumph.

books.title: The Daily Stoic
books.author: Ryan Holiday & Stephen Hanselman
books.description: A year of Stoicism, one page per day: a passage from Marcus Aurelius, Seneca, or Epictetus with a short modern commentary, organized by the disciplines of perception, action, and will.

books.title: Meditations
books.author: Marcus Aurelius
books.description: The private notebooks of Rome's philosopher-emperor, written in Greek on campaign and never meant for publication — a working discipline of attention, mortality, and duty. Gregory Hays's Modern Library translation is the modern standard: spare, direct, and the version most often recommended.

books.title: The Samson Syndrome
books.author: Mark Atteberry
books.description: Why do some strong men fail while others succeed? Atteberry reads the story of Samson — the Bible's strongest man, brought down by his own appetites — as a field guide to the twelve tendencies that shipwreck powerful men, from disregarding boundaries to losing sight of the big picture.

books.title: King, Warrior, Magician, Lover
books.author: Robert Moore & Douglas Gillette
books.description: Two Jungian analysts map the mature masculine into four archetypes — the King who orders and blesses, the Warrior who acts, the Magician who knows, the Lover who connects — and show what each looks like in its fullness and in its shadow. The full title: Rediscovering the Archetypes of the Mature Masculine.

books.title: No More Mr. Nice Guy
books.author: Robert A. Glover
books.description: A therapist's recovery plan for Nice Guy Syndrome — men who seek everyone's approval, hide their needs behind covert contracts, and end up frustrated and stuck. Glover's program: stop performing goodness, state your needs directly, set boundaries, and reclaim your masculine edge.

books.title: How Emotions Are Made
books.author: Lisa Feldman Barrett
books.description: A leading neuroscientist overturns the classical view of emotion: emotions are not universal reflexes hardwired into separate brain regions but predictions your brain constructs from bodily sensations, past experience, and culture — a revolution with consequences for health, law, and self-knowledge.

books.title: Seven and a Half Lessons About the Brain
books.author: Lisa Feldman Barrett
books.description: Seven short essays — and a half — on what the brain actually is: not a reaction machine with a rational rider on top, but a prediction organ that evolved to run the body's budget. Barrett retires the lizard-brain myth and rebuilds the basics in two hundred brisk pages.

books.title: Brainwashed: Challenging the Myth of Black Inferiority
books.author: Tom Burrell
books.description: An advertising legend turns his own tools on the industry that made him. Burrell — founder of Burrell Communications, the agency that changed how America markets to Black consumers — argues that centuries of propaganda sold a myth of Black inferiority so effectively that its targets internalized it, and lays out how to undo the brainwash.

books.title: Parable of the Sower
books.author: Octavia E. Butler
books.description: In a 2020s California of walled neighborhoods, drought, and a drug that makes its users worship fire, teenager Lauren Olamina — who feels others' pain and pleasure as her own — founds a new faith for a collapsing world: Earthseed, whose God is Change. The first of Butler's Parable novels, and her most prophetic.

books.title: Thinking in Systems
books.author: Donella H. Meadows
books.description: Meadows' primer on how systems actually behave: stocks, flows, feedback loops, and the traps (policy resistance, shifting burdens) that make well-meant fixes backfire.

books.title: The Fifth Discipline
books.author: Peter M. Senge
books.description: Senge's classic on the learning organization: five disciplines, with systems thinking as the fifth that integrates the rest, and the archetypes that explain recurring organizational behavior.

books.title: Complexity: A Guided Tour
books.author: Melanie Mitchell
books.description: A Santa Fe Institute tour of complexity science: how ant colonies, immune systems, economies, and the web produce large-scale order from simple local interactions.

books.title: The Black Swan
books.author: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
books.description: Taleb on the events that drive history: unpredictable, massive in impact, and explained away afterward as if they had been foreseeable all along.

books.title: The Fifth Risk
books.author: Michael Lewis
books.description: Lewis tours the federal departments most Americans never think about, and the slow, invisible risk that accumulates when the people who run them stop being taken seriously.

books.title: Recoding America
books.author: Jennifer Pahlka
books.description: The founder of Code for America on why government fails in the digital age: policy written without delivery in mind, and how to rebuild the state's capacity to implement.

books.title: Prisoners of Geography
books.author: Tim Marshall
books.description: Ten maps that explain world politics: how mountains, rivers, plains, and ports constrain what nations can do, whatever their leaders intend.

books.title: How Big Things Get Done
books.author: Bent Flyvbjerg & Dan Gardner
books.description: Flyvbjerg's database of 16,000 projects explains why big things run late and over budget — optimism, uniqueness bias, haste — and the discipline of thinking slow and acting fast.

books.title: Powered by Projects
books.author: Antonio Nieto-Rodriguez
books.description: Nieto-Rodriguez argues the project economy has already arrived: organizations now create value through projects, not operations, and leadership has to be rebuilt around that fact.

books.title: Team of Teams
books.author: Stanley McChrystal
books.description: McChrystal rebuilt a hierarchical task force into a network — shared consciousness, radical transparency, decentralized authority — to fight an enemy that already worked that way.

books.title: Inside the Box
books.author: Drew Boyd & Jacob Goldenberg
books.description: Systematic Inventive Thinking: creativity as a discipline of working inside the box — subtract, multiply, divide, unify, and depend — rather than waiting for inspiration outside it.

books.title: Think Wrong
books.author: John Bielenberg, Mike Burn, Greg Galle & Elizabeth Evitts Dickinson
books.description: A field guide to conquering the status quo: six practices — be bold, get out, let go, make stuff, bet small, move fast — for producing solutions the usual thinking cannot reach.

books.title: The Medici Effect
books.author: Frans Johansson
books.description: Breakthrough ideas live at intersections — of fields, cultures, and industries — and Johansson shows how to put yourself where those collisions happen on purpose.

books.title: Being Logical
books.author: D. Q. McInerny
books.description: A short, lucid primer on thinking straight: preparing the mind for logic, building an argument from premises to conclusion, and spotting the fallacies that derail both.

books.title: The Art of Asking Essential Questions
books.author: Linda Elder & Richard Paul
books.description: Elder and Paul on the skill underneath all learning: asking analytic and evaluative questions that surface assumptions, test conclusions, and expose what a thinker does not yet know.

books.title: How to Read Paintings
books.author: Liz Rideal
books.description: A crash course in reading Western painting: composition, medium, signs and symbols, worked through fifty artworks from da Vinci to Van Gogh.

books.title: How to Live
books.author: Sarah Bakewell
books.description: Montaigne's life told as one question — how to live — in twenty attempts at an answer: pay attention, read a lot, reflect, and keep a private room of one's own.

books.title: The Knowledge: How to Rebuild Civilization in the Aftermath of a Cataclysm
books.author: Lewis Dartnell
books.description: Dartnell's reboot manual for civilization: the agriculture, chemistry, materials, and medicine you would need to restart the world after a collapse — and a tour of how much knowledge modern life quietly depends on.

books.title: The Making of the Atomic Bomb
books.author: Richard Rhodes
books.description: Rhodes' Pulitzer-winning history of the bomb: from the first splitting of the atom through Los Alamos to Hiroshima, told through the scientists who saw what was coming and built it anyway.

books.title: The Information: A History, a Theory, a Flood
books.author: James Gleick
books.description: Gleick traces information from African talking drums through Morse, Babbage, and Shannon to the modern flood: how a substance nobody could see became the thing civilization runs on — and drowns in.

books.title: The Invention of Nature: Alexander von Humboldt's New World
books.author: Andrea Wulf
books.description: Wulf recovers Alexander von Humboldt, the forgotten father of environmentalism: the first to see nature as a living web, connecting climate, vegetation, and human damage across continents.

books.title: Seeing Like a State: How Certain Schemes to Improve the Human Condition Have Failed
books.author: James C. Scott
books.description: Scott on why grand schemes to improve the human condition so often fail: states simplify living societies into legible grids, then mistake the map for the territory — and crush the local knowledge that made things work.

books.title: The Box: How the Shipping Container Made the World Smaller and the World Economy Bigger
books.author: Marc Levinson
books.description: Levinson tells how a plain steel box — the shipping container — cut the cost of moving goods by more than ninety percent and quietly remade ports, cities, and the entire world economy.

books.title: The Master and His Emissary: The Divided Brain and the Making of the Western World
books.author: Iain McGilchrist
books.description: McGilchrist argues the brain's two hemispheres attend to the world in rival ways — one grasping the whole, one seizing the parts — and that Western culture has increasingly handed authority to the wrong one.

books.title: Structures: Or Why Things Don't Fall Down
books.author: J.E. Gordon
books.description: Gordon explains, with wit and almost no mathematics, why bridges stand, dams hold, and knees work: stress, strain, elasticity, and the safety margins built into everything from cathedrals to kangaroos.

books.title: Metaphors We Live By
books.author: George Lakoff & Mark Johnson
books.description: Lakoff and Johnson's classic argument that metaphor is not decoration but the machinery of thought itself: we understand arguments as war, time as money, and ideas as objects — and those framings steer what we do.

books.title: Impro: Improvisation and the Theatre
books.author: Keith Johnstone
books.description: Johnstone's landmark on improvisation: status games, spontaneity, and narrative skill — why we block our own imaginations, and the exercises that unblock them. A theatre book that reads as a manual for creative life.

books.title: The Horse, the Wheel, and Language: How Bronze-Age Riders from the Eurasian Steppes Shaped the Modern World
books.author: David W. Anthony
books.description: Anthony solves a two-century puzzle — where the Indo-European languages came from — by joining archaeology to linguistics: steppe riders who tamed the horse and built the wheel, and spread a language family now spoken by half the world.

books.title: The Visual Display of Quantitative Information
books.author: Edward R. Tufte
books.description: Tufte's founding text of data visualization: data-ink, chartjunk, small multiples, and the ethics of showing numbers honestly — the Strunk & White of graphs, printed as beautifully as it preaches.

books.title: The Psychology of Money
books.author: Morgan Housel
books.description: Nineteen short stories on the strange ways people think about wealth, greed, and happiness — why doing well with money has less to do with what you know than with how you behave.

books.title: Profit First
books.author: Mike Michalowicz
books.description: Michalowicz flips the oldest formula in business: instead of Sales − Expenses = Profit, take the profit first and let expenses fit what remains. A cash-management system of separate accounts that makes a company profitable by design rather than by hope.

books.title: Unshakeable
books.author: Tony Robbins
books.description: Robbins' financial freedom playbook, distilled from interviews with fifty of the world's leading investors: keep fees low, prepare for the correction instead of fearing it, diversify, and let compounding do the heavy lifting. A steady hand for turbulent markets.

mentalModels.name: First Principles Thinking
mentalModels.summary: Break a problem down to its most fundamental truths and reason up from there.

mentalModels.name: Compounding
mentalModels.summary: Small, consistent gains accumulate exponentially over time.

mentalModels.name: Inversion
mentalModels.summary: Solve problems backward — figure out what you want to avoid, then avoid it.

mentalModels.name: Second-Order Thinking
mentalModels.summary: Consider the consequences of the consequences, not just the immediate result.

mentalModels.name: Occam's Razor
mentalModels.summary: Among competing explanations, the simplest is usually the best.

mentalModels.name: System 1 / System 2
mentalModels.summary: The mind runs on a fast, intuitive system and a slow, deliberate one.

mentalModels.name: Loss Aversion
mentalModels.summary: Losses feel roughly twice as painful as equivalent gains feel good.

mentalModels.name: Map Is Not the Territory
mentalModels.summary: Our models of reality are not reality itself — beware confusing them.

mentalModels.name: Circle of Competence
mentalModels.summary: Know the boundaries of what you actually understand, and act inside them.

mentalModels.name: Opportunity Cost
mentalModels.summary: The true cost of a choice is the best alternative you gave up.

mentalModels.name: Hanlon's Razor
mentalModels.summary: Never attribute to malice that which is adequately explained by stupidity.

mentalModels.name: Narrative Fallacy
mentalModels.summary: We invent tidy stories to explain messy, random events after the fact.

mentalModels.name: Incentives
mentalModels.summary: Behavior follows what is actually rewarded, not what is preached — find the incentive and you can predict the outcome.

mentalModels.name: Feedback Loops
mentalModels.summary: A system's outputs circle back as its inputs: reinforcing loops compound change, balancing loops hold things steady.

mentalModels.name: Emergence
mentalModels.summary: Complex order arises from simple rules repeated at scale — no single part plans the whole.

mentalModels.name: Social Proof
mentalModels.summary: We copy what the people around us visibly do — imitation is the mind's shortcut for deciding what is normal, safe, and worth wanting.

mentalModels.name: Hormesis
mentalModels.summary: A measured dose of stress makes a system stronger — muscle, bone, immunity, and character grow under load and weaken under total shelter.

mentalModels.name: Margin of Safety
mentalModels.summary: Build buffers before you need them: families, budgets, and projects break at the margin, not on the average day.

mentalModels.name: Power Laws
mentalModels.summary: Outcomes follow a steep curve, not a bell curve: a few causes drive most results, and the extremes outweigh the average.

mentalModels.name: The Adjacent Possible
mentalModels.summary: What can be built next is bounded by what already exists — new ideas arrive one reachable step at a time, and each step opens the next set of doors.

mentalModels.name: Exaptation
mentalModels.summary: A trait built for one job gets recruited for another — feathers evolved for warmth become feathers for flight; the use you find is not always the use intended.

mentalModels.name: Consilience
mentalModels.summary: When independent fields arrive at the same answer by different roads, confidence compounds — truth is what survives being approached from several directions.

mentalModels.name: The Lindy Effect
mentalModels.summary: What has already lasted a long time is likely to keep lasting — time is a filter: the durable outlives the fashionable, and age itself becomes evidence.

mentalModels.name: Antifragility
mentalModels.summary: Some systems don't merely survive stress — they improve from it. Where the fragile break and the robust endure, the antifragile treat volatility as information and grow.

mentalModels.name: Natural Selection
mentalModels.summary: Variation, selection, time: what persists is not what is perfect but what fits its environment — change the environment and you change what survives in it.

mentalModels.name: Adaptation
mentalModels.summary: Living things reshape themselves to their niche — behavior follows environment far more reliably than it follows intention, in animals, children, and organizations alike.

mentalModels.name: Ecosystems
mentalModels.summary: Nothing exists alone: outcomes emerge from webs of relationship, not isolated parts — pull one thread and the whole system moves.

mentalModels.name: The Niche
mentalModels.summary: Every species thrives by occupying a role that isn't already taken — head-on competition with a stronger incumbent is nature's most expensive strategy; differentiation is the cheapest.

mentalModels.name: Carrying Capacity
mentalModels.summary: Every environment caps the growth it can support — populations, projects, and schedules that overshoot don't plateau, they crash.

mentalModels.name: Red Queen Effect
mentalModels.summary: In a coevolving system you must keep adapting just to hold your place, because everything around you is adapting too — standing still is a decision to fall behind.

mentalModels.name: Diversity as Insurance
mentalModels.summary: Monocultures are efficient and fragile; diverse systems survive shocks that wipe out uniform ones — variation is the premium you pay for resilience.
